thread:
kiran (customer): Hey, upgraded our app to use @redwood-js/sdk v1.0.0 (ts client) and now requests to the chat/stream endpoint return 404. Works fine with v0.9.2. Any ideas?

elena (support): Sorry you're hitting that, can you paste the exact error and the request payload you used?

kiran (customer): Error from node: `UnhandledPromiseRejection: HTTPError: 404 Not Found - /v1/chat/stream`
Request snippet (TS):
```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-alpha', input: 'hello' });
```

mia (support-engineer): Hmm, are you using the `chat.stream` helper or `chat.completions`? v1 landed some breaking renames in the client. Can you `console.log(client._version)`?

kiran (customer): version prints `1.0.0`

elena (support): Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) can you share Node/npm versions, and 2) any proxy or custom baseUrl?

kiran (customer): node 18.16.0, npm 9.6.7, no proxy, default base url.

jordan (eng): @elena @mia ping — I remember we changed route names in the TS SDK to align with the API surface. There was discussion about `chat.stream` vs `chat.streams` and `model` -> `model_name`. Looks like the client released the call wrapper but the server still expects the old param. We might have a mismatch between client v1.0.0 and server routing on the hosted infra.

tyler (devex): @kiran as a quick repro, can you try raw fetch to the endpoint that used to work? e.g.:
```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-alpha', input: 'hello' })
})
  .then(r => r.text()).then(console.log)
```

kiran (customer): Raw fetch to /v1/chat/stream returns 404 as well. Response body: `{"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"endpoint not found"}}`.

mia (support-engineer): Ok so server-side routing doesn't have that path right now. @jordan any rollout notes? Could be partial deployment in region causing 404s.

jordan (eng): We rolled a router change yesterday that renamed `chat/stream` -> `chat/streams` and also swapped `model` -> `model_name` in the request schema. The plan was to keep a compatibility proxy for one week, but looks like that proxy didn't deploy to prod in us-west. We need to either restore the proxy or patch clients.

elena (support): For immediate mitigation for you @kiran: two options — 1) pin to SDK 0.9.2 (npm i @redwood-inference/sdk@0.9.2) until we fix infra; or 2) call the new endpoint explicitly (if you want to stay on v1.0.0) by hitting `/v1/chat/streams` and using `model_name` param. Example raw payload:
```json
{ "model_name": "redwood-alpha", "input": "hello" }
```

kiran (customer): I tried calling `/v1/chat/streams` with `model_name` and got 400: `Unknown parameter: model_name` so seems server wants `model` in our region. This smells like partial rollout yes.

jordan (eng): Confirmed — can reproduce in us-west. Prod rollout was incomplete; ingress rules still point to old service in eu-central but new service in us-west. I'll open an incident to roll back the rename in us-west or re-add the compatibility proxy.

redwood-bot: Incident created #INC-2026 by jordan: "partial router rename causing TS SDK v1.0.0 break"

tyler (devex): We'll also push a short doc note and sample migration snippet for customers. Proposed client-side compatibility shim for anyone who can't pin old SDK quickly:
```ts
// shim to normalize v1.0.0 calls back to old params
function normalizePayload(payload){
  if (payload.model_name) { payload.model = payload.model_name; delete payload.model_name; }
  return payload;
}
client.chat.stream = async (p) => fetch(`${client.baseUrl}/v1/chat/stream`, { method: 'POST', headers: client.headers, body: JSON.stringify(normalizePayload(p)) });
```

mia (support-engineer): Action items: 1) eng will restore compatibility proxy in us-west (jordan) 2) publish patch or hotfix to v1.0.1 if needed (jordan/tyler) 3) support note to customers with repro + workaround (elena/mia) 4) follow-up @kiran once fixed.

elena (support): Kiran — sorry for the disruption. We'll update this thread when the proxy is live. In the meantime, if you're blocked we recommend pinning to 0.9.2 or using the shim above.

kiran (customer): Thanks, appreciate the quick turn. Will pin for now and wait for your update. :thumbsup:
